title: Define acceptance contracts for variable scope and rollback matrices
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Upcoming Private deployment introduces a modular PRD where some features are mandatory (core runtime changes) and others are optional (observability enhancements, advanced caching heuristics). Past rollouts lacked explicit, machine-readable acceptance contracts which led to ambiguous go decisions and two unplanned rollbacks. Goal: Define a cross-team (PM/Eng/Design/Legal/Security) set of acceptance contracts and a rollback matrix that maps observed signals to action steps and owners. The contract should support variable-scope PRDs: allow shipping with optional features gated but ensure core safety and SLO guarantees before any customer-facing expansion.
scope: Draft formal acceptance contract template (core vs optional buckets)
Define a three-tier rollback matrix (inform, mitigate, rollback) with concrete thresholds and owners
Create litmus tests (automated and manual) that each team signs off on before progressive rollout steps
Integrate acceptance checkpoints into PRD checklist and Console rollout UI (links to toggles)
Document legal/consent copy and data residency acknowledgements required for private customers
out_of_scope: Automated enforcement of contract in CI (follow-up ticket)
Full telemetry instrumentation work (assumes ENG-8412 completes core traces)
Rewriting existing runbooks across unrelated services
proposal: Use a 2-bucket acceptance contract: CORE (must pass) and EXTENSIONAL (optional, can be toggled off)
Each contract item must include: owner, test artifact (link to test or script), pass criteria, rollback trigger, mitigations
Rollback matrix: Level 1 (monitor) / Level 2 (throttle + mitigation) / Level 3 (full rollback); map signals (errors, latency, cost delta, legal flags) to actions
Require legal signoff for any customer-facing wording and for changes that affect telemetry or PII even if marked EXTENSIONAL
Publish contract as a single-page checklist attached to the PRD (Confluence) and a GitHub issue template for release engineers
acceptance_criteria: A single acceptance contract template exists in Confluence and is linked from the PRD
Engineering provides automated litmus tests and example run commands; tests can be executed in staging within 2 hours
Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail for representative private workload must not regress by more than 5% for CORE changes under canary load (1% traffic)
Error budget: No new customer-facing error class above severity P1 observed during canary; any P1 requires immediate mitigation
KV cache cold-start: median warm-up below 120ms for core model-serving path in staging
Legal: Approved customer-facing copy and telemetry data handling statement for the feature; any open legal issues must be explicitly listed in the contract
Rollout plan: Canary cadence documented (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with explicit wait-times and telemetry checks between steps
Rollback triggers enumerated and mapped to owners with contact methods (pager/team) and runbook links
success_metrics: First production rollout follows the contract and completes without Level 3 rollback
Time from canary start to full rollout under 10 working days for CORE-only launches
Number of rollbacks for related PRDs reduced by 60% in 6 months
Clear traceability: 100% of PRDs for private deployment attach a signed acceptance contract before release
